trends.name: Iran Oil Disruption Crisis
trends.summary: Iran attacks on Saudi pipeline and production facilities have triggered massive oil supply disruption. OPEC+ production fell record 20.5% (9M bpd loss) in March; Strait of Hormuz flows down 92% from normal levels with Brent crude at worst weekly drop since 2022. Trump demanding reopening of strait as U.S.-Iran weekend negotiations loom with existential geopolitical risk to energy markets.

trends.name: AI Productivity Paradox
trends.summary: AI adoption will boost long-term productivity but drag economy down in near term—creating near-term headwinds before gains materialize. Meta and Salesforce showing divergent AI positioning, with market reassessing how AI capex translates to actual returns and enterprise revenue growth.

trends.name: Record Global M&A Boom
trends.summary: Global dealmaking surged 18% YoY to $1.25 trillion in Q1 2026—the largest Q1 on record—including mega-deals like Unilever's $44.8B food sale and Sysco's $29.1B transaction. Insider buying also at 5-month highs (26.4%), signaling confidence despite geopolitical tensions.

trends.name: S&P 500 Momentum & Technical Setup
trends.summary: $SPY on 8-day winning streak with weekly closes above 50dma and 200dma for third consecutive week—best RSI in 3 months. VIX signal flashing unusual pattern suggesting S&P 500 could reach 7,400 within months, though weekend geopolitical talks pose critical risk.

trends.name: U.S.-EU Tech Regulation Tensions
trends.summary: Trump administration escalating anger over EU Big Tech fines totaling $7 billion in 2 years, signaling coming trade friction and regulatory conflict between U.S. and European tech enforcement. Market impact on multinational tech exposure and potential tariff/retaliatory measures.

trends.name: Chip Demand Resilience Despite Tensions
trends.summary: TSMC reports forecast-beating revenue as AI chip demand continues strong despite geopolitical tensions with China. Micron also upgraded on cyclical fears crushing. AI chip demand remains the most resilient macro driver even amid Taiwan/China tensions.

trends.name: Inflation Holding Steady at 3.3%
trends.summary: Consumer prices rose 3.3% in March as expected, maintaining elevated inflation above Fed's 2% target. Combined with wage growth data showing lower-income households gaining traction post-2022, inflation dynamics remain key rate-hold anchor for Fed policy through summer.

trends.name: Fed Chair Nomination Uncertainty
trends.summary: Kevin Warsh's Fed chair confirmation hearing delayed, creating policy uncertainty at critical moment with geopolitical shocks, inflation persistence, and rate trajectory in question. Leadership vacuum complicates near-term monetary policy response to oil crisis.

trends.name: Emerging Markets & International Equities Rally
trends.summary: VXUS rated Strong Buy and EWY (South Korea ETF) showing rally continuation as strategists advocate international equity exposure as hedge against U.S.-centric tech concentration. Global chaos normalizing international diversification as portfolio essential.

trends.name: Insurance Industry Stress Warnings
trends.summary: Insurance ratings firm warns industry may not survive next financial crisis as robustly as it did in 2008-09, signaling potential vulnerabilities in balance sheets and reserves amid rate volatility and geopolitical claims exposure.

trends.name: Consumer Spending Pressure & Wage Inequality
trends.summary: Despite wage growth for lower-income households, real purchasing power strained—bag of Doritos now $7 while minimum wage stagnant at $7.25. Young people drinking less (major winemaker turning to hard liquor) signals consumer spending rebalancing and discretionary weakness.

trends.name: China-Taiwan Tensions & Cross-Strait Talks
trends.summary: Xi Jinping invokes 'threat' of Taiwan independence in first cross-strait opposition talks in decade, while China actively negotiates Iran ceasefire (business over politics). Taiwan risk and geopolitical complexity now pricing into semiconductor and supply chain strategies.
